extracted.intended_audience: applicants preparing and submitting paper PHS 398 research project grant applications to NIH and other PHS/PHS agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required standards for preparing and submitting paper Research Project Grant applications using the PHS 398 form to NIH and other PHS agencies (non-electronic submissions). Covers format, required attachments, content of Research Plan, biosketch, budget, human subjects, select agents, consortiums, appendix rules, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a succinct Research Plan and follow Table of Page Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a succinct Research Plan and follow the Table of Page Limits unless the FOA specifies otherwise. Sections 4-11 of the Research Plan have no maximum allowable pages, but should also be succinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are explicitly reminded to be concise; follow FOA-specific exceptions if provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must be complete and accurate at time of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a complete application. The application must be complete and accurate at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may not be reviewed if incomplete, illegible, fail to follow instructions, or present insufficient material to permit an adequate review; no guarantee SRO/reviewers will accept additional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to font, margin, and legibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adherence to font and margin requirements is necessary; no applicant should have an advantage by using smaller, denser type; small type sizes may make it difficult for reviewers to read the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CSR Division of Receipt and Referral has responsibility to make the final determination of legibility and authority to return applications. That decision is final and not subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration processes required (eRA Commons, institutional registrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, institutions, and PD/PIs must complete required registrations prior to applying (see Prepare to Apply-Register).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register organization, Signing Official, PD/PIs, and other users with eRA Commons and other systems as instructed; see eRA Service Desk and Prepare to Apply resources for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact PHS staff before submission and follow assignment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are strongly encouraged to communicate with PHS staff throughout application, review and award process to identify appropriate IC/SRG and get advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact GrantsInfo, Division of Receipt and Referral, Program Staff, or SRO as appropriate; requests for assignment or reassignment should be submitted in writing to DRR; do not contact reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must never contact reviewers regarding their applications because discussion of the scientific content or attempted influence will create serious breaches of confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are required to notify the SRO if contacted by an applicant; communication may delay review or result in return of application without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit identical or essentially identical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions of identical applications to one or more components of the PHS are not allowed; similar/essentially identical grant applications with essentially the same research focus from the same applicant organization for the same due date will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are strictly enumerated (e.g., K02 with identical research to a research project; certain resubmissions); identical/essentially identical submissions may be delayed or not reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission application materials are those submitted after submission but prior to initial peer review; policy accepts only materials resulting from an unforeseen event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-submission materials can only be submitted as a PDF attachment; SRO uploads acceptable materials into the official electronic grant file; applicants can view additions via eRA Commons 'Additions for Review'. See NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 2.3.7.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include a cover letter with the competing application; place the letter at the beginning of the original application; do not copy it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter is for internal agency use only and will not be shared with peer reviewers. It may include application title, FOA title, reasons for late submission, explanations for changed/corrected applications, agency approval documentation for certain application types (e.g., $500,000+), intent to submit a video, statements about generating large-scale genomic data, or assignment requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of copies, original signature, and single-sided requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the original and two identical, legible, single-sided photocopies of each application. The original must be signed by an Authorized Organization Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make copies after signature so the official’s signature is present on the copies; do not staple or otherwise bind the original or copies; use rubber bands or clips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bindings, packaging, and appendix CDs
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit all materials in one package: cover letter (original only), original application, two copies, and appendix materials — two identical CDs of all appendix material in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label each disk with PD/PI name and application title; do not use compression or password protection; if burning on Mac use ISO 9660 format; do not include more than one application in each mailing envelope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix allowed materials and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices must be submitted on CDs (two identical); a maximum of 10 PDF attachments allowed; only limited items are allowed in the Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed items: blank data collection forms/screenshots, simple lists of interview questions, blank informed consent/assent forms, and other items only if specified in the FOA. Do not include data, data compilations, analyses, publications, manuals, or MTAs unless FOA allows. Noncompliant appendix materials may cause withdrawal and non-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face Page completion and authorized signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Face Page of the PHS 398 and include required signature by Authorized Organization Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original application must include the required signature on the Face Page; copies should be made after signature so they include it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary and Relevance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Summary and Relevance section as part of the application (Project Summary and Relevance, Project/Performance Sites, Senior/Key Personnel, Other Significant Contributors...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Summary should succinctly describe the proposed research and its relevance to public health; follow the specific Face Page and summary instructions in Section 4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow updated Biographical Sketch instructions; scholastic performance requires only scientific/professional graduate courses to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Biographical Sketches for key personnel and other applicable personnel; include Other Support information as required (see 4.6.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget preparation and specific budget instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the Budget for the entire proposed project period (Direct Costs Only) and follow Budget Instructions and format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include justification for budgets; certain awards/requested amounts ($500,000 or more) may require prior approval and should be noted in the cover letter with supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Personnel Report and Resources section
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the All Personnel Report and describe institutional/organizational resources in the Resources section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all personnel, roles, and provide descriptions of facilities, equipment, and institutional resources that will support the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan format and required components
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Research Plan format and include required components: Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Bibliography and References Cited/Progress Report Publication List; Vertebrate Animals; Select Agent Research; Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plans; Authentication of Key Resources; PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Research Plan format in 5.4.1 and include required attachments; be succinct even where no page limit applies; follow FOA-specific instructions if they conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Specific Aims section in the Research Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the objectives and hypotheses succinctly and clearly; follow page limits and format guidance in the Table of Page Limits and Section 5.5.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Research Strategy describing the rationale, approach, and methods for the proposed studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some Research Plan sections have no maximum pages, the Research Strategy should be succinct and provide sufficient detail for peer review (see Section 5.5.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography and References Cited / Progress Report Publication List
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Bibliography and References Cited and, where applicable, a Progress Report Publication List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow format instructions and include only relevant citations; use the designated section (5.5.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals compliance and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If vertebrate animals are involved, include required information addressing animal welfare, use of animals, and applicable assurances/worksheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NIH Vertebrate Animals Section Worksheet and NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 4.1.1; provide required documentation such as Animal Welfare Assurance if the grantee institution does not have one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If select agents are proposed, provide a Select Agent Research attachment addressing identification, exclusion status, or application for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each site where select agent research occurs, address (1) identify the Select Agent(s) to be used; (2) provide registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used (identify foreign country for foreign sites); (3) describe all facilities where Select Agent(s) will be used, procedures for monitoring possession/use/transfer, biosafety/biocontainment/security plans, and biocontainment resources available. Be succinct; no specific page limit but concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple PD/PIs are proposed, include a Leadership Plan describing rationale for multiple PD/PI approach and delineating governance and organizational structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe communication plans, processes for decision-making on scientific direction, procedures for resolving conflicts, roles and responsibilities (administrative, technical, scientific), and planned budget allocation if any. In event of award, allocations may be reflected in Notice of Grant Award footnote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium / Contractual Arrangements description
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain programmatic, fiscal, and administrative arrangements between applicant organization and consortium organization(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If consortium activities represent a significant portion of the project, explain why applicant organization rather than the ultimate performer should be grantee; signature on Face Page signifies understanding of consortium policy; see NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach letters of support demonstrating support of consortium participants and collaborators, including Senior/Key Personnel and Other Significant Contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should stipulate expectations for co-authorship, whether promised cell lines/samples/resources are freely available or restricted, for consultants include rate/charge and anticipated level of effort/hours per budget period, and letters are not required for personnel not contributing substantively. Do not include consultant bios in Letters of Support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data, Model Organisms, Genomic Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Resource Sharing Plan(s) as applicable: Data Sharing Plan for applicants seeking $500,000+ in direct costs; Sharing Model Organisms plan; Genomic Data Sharing (GDS) plan for large-scale genomic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data Sharing Plan: brief 1-paragraph description or explanation why not possible; Model Organisms: describe specific plan for sharing distribution of unique model organisms; GDS: include plan for sharing large-scale genomic data and note that institutional certification may be submitted at application but is requested as Just-in-Time prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, briefly describe methods to ensure identity and validity of key biological and/or chemical resources used in the proposed studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A maximum of one page is suggested. Key resources include cell lines, specialty chemicals, antibodies, and other biologics that may differ across labs/time and could influence data. Standard reagents not expected to vary need not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the separate fillable PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information PDF form; it is separate from the Research Plan but part of the overall application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper form lacks pre-population and electronic validations present in electronic system; complete all required sections; certain sections only apply if answering 'Yes' to Are Human Subjects Involved?

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist items and required administrative assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the Checklist form page including items such as Inventions and Patents (renewal apps only), Program Income, Assurances/Certifications, and F&A/Indirect Costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions, indicate whether any were conceived/reduced to practice and whether previously reported; institutions must report inventions to appropriate NIH office per 37 CFR 401.14; indicate F&A rates and if provisional rate used describe process. Foreign institutions may request limited F&A (8% of modified total direct costs less equipment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention reporting and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report inventions conceived or reduced to practice during the course of the project and indicate whether previously reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH recipient organizations must promptly report inventions to the Extramural Inventions and Technology Resources Branch and are encouraged to use iEdison.gov; follow NIH Grants Policy Statement Section 8.4.1.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications after peer review and use of Summary Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: After peer review, PD/PI should review the Summary Statement in eRA Commons and may contact the appropriate awarding component program official to discuss review outcome and obtain guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary Statement and Peer Review Outcome Letter are accessed through eRA Commons only; contacting program official may help clarify numerical human subjects/vertebrate animal designations and funding status; paper copies are not mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA-specific instructions where they differ from PHS 398
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow instructions in the FOA if they conflict with these PHS 398 instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some FOAs may have different instructions for Appendix, page limits, or other submission details; FOA supersedes PHS 398 in case of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and submission mailing instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include more than one application per mailing envelope; assemble pages in order specified in the table of contents; original application must be single-sided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include original cover letter at beginning of original application only; do not duplicate cover letter in copies; rubber bands or clips acceptable; do not staple or bind.
